A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Memory Mosaics at scale. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results on language benchmarks, RULER question answering, and three classification tasks, plus appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds architectural controls, fine-tuning results, and further evaluations. Its separately attributed tables reproducing prior work do not change this assessment.

M1.justification: Equations (8)–(9) change unit-normalized keys and values to features multiplied by learned scales alpha_phi and alpha_psi. Table 6 also replaces the stated uncapped bandwidth reparameterization with capped exponentials. These are limited revisions to the reported model specification; stochastic memory overlap already appeared in v1 Appendix D.

E1.justification: v2 adds the simple needle-retrieval scenario RULER S-NIAH in Table 13. The training coverage, existing language benchmarks, multi-document question answering, and semantic/anonymous classification tasks are retained. The fine-tuning study reuses the existing RULER task.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds Transformer small with long-short-term attention to the anonymous-label Tacred comparison. Existing Transformer and public-model comparator sets remain. Appendix D's reproduced RWKV/Mamba comparisons provide contextual evidence rather than new head-to-head evaluations against Memory Mosaics.

E3.justification: v2 adds a fine-tuning optimization-step sweep for 4k-to-32k adaptation and control conditions involving long-short-term attention and stochastic memory overlap. The previously stated main model scales, training-token budgets, context lengths, and prompt-selection procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained long-term-memory removal ablations, v2 adds a Transformer architectural control (Figure 5), stochastic-overlap ablation (Table 12), fine-tuning-speed analysis (Figure 8), and accuracy-versus-resource analysis (Figure 12). These substantially expand the questions examined about mechanism, adaptation, and computational cost.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments retain point-result reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including a reported 22-percentage-point improvement after one fine-tuning minibatch and 32k extrapolation accuracy of 15.9 versus 31.7 without versus with stochastic overlap. It also adds S-NIAH and architectural-control results. Table 1 corrects the small Memory Mosaics model's MATH/MBPP/RACE-middle entries from 9.4/49.2/1.1 to 1.1/9.4/49.2; the main RULER tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes through the scaled feature definitions in Equations (8)–(9) and the relaxation from beta_0 > 0 to beta_0 >= 0 below Equation (6). The conditional-expectation and kernel-regression reasoning is retained. New Equation (10) merely expands the existing short-window retrieval operation; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three listed contributions, and closing discussion retain the same headline claims: successful scaling, comparable persistent-knowledge performance, and stronger new-task learning, including comparison with an eight-trillion-token Transformer. The additional studies do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking stochastic overlap to allocation of position-invariant information and arguing that long-short-term attention alone does not explain the architectural advantage. Appendix D qualifies the rejection of compression baselines by acknowledging their persistent-knowledge and efficiency strengths; Appendix E clarifies the limits of the efficiency discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplements the existing training recipe with initialization and reparameterization details (Table 6), output concatenation/projection details, and a repository link. Table 11 newly discloses generation limits of 32 tokens for Memory Mosaics versus 128 for public baselines. Expanded prompt descriptions elaborate practices already described in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang's 2025 work, AI for the open-world: the learning principles. It also expands positioning against Transformers and memory-compression approaches, using reproduced results from already cited Hsieh and Li papers. Most references and the broader research framing remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the fine-tuning section, reorganizes appendices, expands selected method and prompt explanations, and makes localized language edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain. The publication footer changes from an under-review preprint to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5, 8, and 12 and several tables covering initialization, reproduced comparisons, ablation, and S-NIAH. It redraws the overlap diagram, replaces several raster classification plots with vector displays and revised labeling, and relocates retained tables and figures. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The new architectural control and stochastic-overlap ablation strengthen support for existing claims, while fine-tuning results, corrected Table 1 entries, and added implementation details improve usefulness and reproducibility. The gains are bounded: uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the resource plots provide sparse documentation of the claimed budget matching. Overall, v2 offers a limited, evidence-supported quality improvement.
